name: Malaysia

findings.summary: U Mobile named Huawei and ZTE as technology partners for Malaysia's second 5G network after a tender to which only those two vendors responded; no contract value or RAN/core split disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 2 (partner selection) rather than tier 3: neither source describes a signed binding contract or value; some trade-blog headlines describe MoUs. Rollout status in 2026 not checked.

findings.summary: Ericsson has supplied the rollout of the state-initiated single wholesale 5G network operated by DNB, launched 2021; the Finance Ministry holds 34% with Maxis, YTL and CelcomDigi holding the rest.
findings.analyst_inference: Single background mention; operational-at-scale tier inferred from DNB's live network. Ericsson contract terms and value not sourced in this pass.

findings.summary: Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching announced 3,000 Huawei Ascend chips would underpin a Malaysian sovereign AI-as-a-service infrastructure with Skyvast and Chinese server maker Leadyo, to be supplied by 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Retracted two days later (MYS-004). Huawei denied selling Ascend chips in Malaysia, per DCD.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI)
findings.reversal_of: MYS-003: deputy minister's announcement of a Huawei Ascend-based sovereign AI initiative
findings.summary: MITI disowned the Huawei/Skyvast AI initiative as not developed, endorsed or coordinated by government, required legal and reputational due diligence for any such project, and reaffirmed export-control compliance; the minister's remarks were retracted.
findings.analyst_inference: Retraction followed US pushback per later reporting (SoyaCincau 2026-09-10); the causal link is reported, not stated by MITI.

findings.summary: Bloomberg, citing anonymous sources, reported Malaysia leaning toward Huawei Ascend 910C chips for a RM2 billion sovereign AI programme whose backbone Telekom Malaysia won by tender; nothing signed, and a separate Nvidia/AMD tender was discussed.
findings.analyst_inference: All three sources relay one Bloomberg report, so not independent; coded tier 1 because it is a reported deliberation, not even an official statement. RM2bn (~US$494m per TNW) is the programme value, not a Huawei award, so left out of value fields. State Dept warned against untrusted suppliers; NSC officials due in Washington.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI)
findings.summary: MITI placed US-origin high-performance AI chips on the Strategic Items List under a catch-all control, requiring a Strategic Trade Permit and 30 days' notice before export, transhipment or transit.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the regime is controlled by Malaysia but exists to align with US export controls against diversion of US chips; it is evidence of US-facing compliance rather than a US- or domestic-controlled asset.

findings.summary: YTL Power declared its YTL AI Cloud facility in Kulai, Johor operational, running liquid-cooled Nvidia GB200 NVL72 Grace Blackwell systems; unit count not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Silicon pole is US (Nvidia controls firmware/driver updates and is subject to US export licensing); facility controller is domestic (MYS-008).

findings.summary: YTL's first AI data centre in its 600 MW Green Data Center Park, Kulai, Johor was completed and is operational, positioned by government as part of Malaysia's sovereign AI effort.
Prime Minister Anwar launched ILMU, a Malaysian multimodal large language model built by YTL AI Labs with Universiti Malaya, presented as a homegrown sovereign model.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 (launched/released) rather than 5: adoption at scale across government not evidenced. Training/serving hardware appears to be the Nvidia-based YTL AI Cloud (MYS-007), so model control is domestic but the compute layer beneath it is US.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI)
findings.summary: Trade minister Tengku Zafrul said ByteDance planned about MYR10 billion to make Malaysia a regional AI hub plus MYR1.5 billion to extend its data-centre footprint; TikTok already has a Johor data centre.
findings.analyst_inference: Announced value uses the source's own conversion (MYR10bn ~ US$2.13bn) and excludes the separate MYR1.5bn. Ministerial announcement only; no construction or contract evidence found in this pass.

findings.summary: DayOne, GDS's international arm, has operated a Johor data-centre campus since about 2023 and in March 2025 was reported seeking a roughly US$3.4bn-equivalent syndicated loan for expansion and refinancing.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: DayOne was the international arm of PRC-listed GDS but has been restructured with outside investors; current controlling jurisdiction is unresolved. Loan closure and tenants (reportedly hyperscale/ByteDance in other press) not verified.

findings.summary: Google announced a US$2 billion (RM9.4 billion) investment for its first Malaysian data centre at Elmina Business Park on Sime Darby Property land and a Greater Kuala Lumpur cloud region.
findings.analyst_inference: Construction progress not checked; global cloud layer still lists the GCP Malaysia region as announced, not live.

findings.local_actor: Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
findings.summary: After meeting China's public security minister, Deputy PM Zahid said Malaysia is ready to consider Chinese-style HD CCTV with facial recognition at crime hotspots, citing an earlier Johor pilot; to be taken to Cabinet, no vendor named.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the statement endorses a Chinese policing model but names no vendor or controller. Bernama is Malaysian state media (S4). Vendor of the earlier Iskandar Puteri pilot unknown.

power.null_reason: no AI-specific power evidence surfaced in data-centre searches; search budget spent on silicon and network layers

research_gaps: Has U Mobile signed binding Huawei/ZTE contracts (RAN vs core, value), and what is its 2026 coverage?
Outcome of the RM2bn sovereign AI programme chip choice (Huawei Ascend 910C vs Nvidia/AMD) and the Telekom Malaysia tender award notice.
Current controlling jurisdiction of DayOne after its restructuring away from GDS, and whether the 2025 loan closed.
Status of Google's Elmina data centre and Microsoft's Malaysia West build-out (construction/operation tier).
ByteDance Malaysia AI hub: any construction or contract evidence beyond the 2024 ministerial statement.
Vendor of the Iskandar Puteri policing CCTV pilot and any Cabinet decision after Zahid's October 2026 China visit.
Government adoption of foreign frontier models (OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen) by ministries — not found in this pass.
